answer: Cross-epoch reputation decay gate: each identity's score updates only from actions whose predicted next-epoch behaviour stays within tolerance, so a sudden shift flags the account. Like a trellis, the rule binds history to future conduct, forcing sockpuppets to age consistently or lose standing. Any ripple from coordinated new accounts gets damped because each must sustain plausible continuity across epochs. An attacker pays continuous labour per identity, since a zephyr of fresh accounts cannot fast-forward the waiting periods.
